summary: Contestants apply accounting principles to record transactions, prepare and analyze financial statements, and evaluate business structures for accurate reporting and informed decision-making. The event includes both objective and application evaluation methods. Any postsecondary division contestant may enter, but cannot enter both College Accounting and Advanced College Accounting in the same year.
time_limits: No more than ten (10) minutes for orientation
No more than ninety (90) minutes for testing
No more than ten (10) minutes for wrap-up
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards. See NLC Calculator Guidelines. Contestants who violate this rule will be disqualified
competencies: Analyze and compare business ownership structures to evaluate strategic, legal, and operational implications
Apply the accounting cycle to record and report financial data in compliance with industry standards and decision-making needs
Apply financial standards to assess and report the value of assets, liabilities, and equity in accordance with GAAP
Interpret foundational accounting concepts and terminology to explain the role of accounting systems in supporting financial accuracy, compliance, and business decision-making
Evaluate, journalize, and post financial transactions to determine their impact on assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, expenses, and dividends in accordance with GAAP
Apply multiple depreciation methods to calculate asset value in compliance with financial reporting standards
Calculate and record end-of-period adjustments to ensure accurate financial reporting and compliance with accrual accounting principles
Maintain inventory records using perpetual accounting systems and apply inventory costing methods to ensure accurate valuation and cost flow analysis
Evaluate and manage credit risk, including estimating and recording uncollectible accounts using data-driven methods
Calculate and analyze interest and maturity values for various financial instruments
Prepare, interpret, and analyze financial statements for service, merchandising, and digital business models
Analyze financial performance using key ratios and dashboards, integrating data visualization tools and benchmarking techniques
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
No equipment, supplies, or materials other than those specified for an event will be allowed in the testing area

Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests or facsimiles (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification.
eligibility_notes: Any postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event.
Contestants may not enter College Accounting and Advanced College Accounting in the same year.
This event may not be repeated.
